sentences.text: The premise holds on this record: all four quarters clear 70%, and the tightest quarter, Q3 FY2026, clears it by 3.4 percentage points, about 1.69x a typical move.
It is a recent condition, not a long-standing one: across 20 filing dates the test held in only 6, and its outcome last changed with the 2026-05-20 filing.
The margin is restored rather than expanding: it sits 0.2 percentage points below where it was 8 quarters ago, with a 60.5% trough in Q1 FY2026 in between.

The filing ties that 60.5% trough to a $4.5 billion H20 inventory and purchase-obligation charge, so the trough is labelled a one-off, but it shows how fast a single charge can take the margin under 70%.

The step from the claim to buying now is that the margin persists, and the price depends on exactly that: the reverse DCF at the 2026-09-30 price assumes a 65.2% operating margin every year, and at the industry's 90th-percentile margin of 26.6% the same price would need 28.1% growth a year instead of 13.4%.
So the claim is true and relevant, but it describes a backward-looking condition the price already assumes; it does not by itself argue that the price is low.
The margin is both high and improving on the comparable quarter: 75.0% against 72.4% a year earlier, which the filing attributes to Blackwell Ultra mix.

Against its industry the level is exceptional, ranked 4 of 63 among SIC 3674 filers against a class median of 41.2%, and the implication that operating margin stayed above 50% in each quarter also came out as the claim implies.
In 69% of resampled paths, drawn from the margin's own past quarterly changes, the test held in each of the next 4 quarters; this is a description of past volatility, not a forecast.

Inventory is building faster than the cost of sales: 119.3 days against 105.6 a year before, with the balance up +111.0% against cost of revenue up +86.8%. That is the same setup that preceded the H20 charge which sank the margin to 60.5%.
In 31% of resampled paths the test did not survive four more quarters, and the cushion is less than two typical moves. One bad quarter would break the claim as worded.
The filing reports a net unfavorable impact of 0.8% on Q2 gross margin, so the 75.0% already carries a drag that the record does not explain.
Whether the margin stays above 70% while inventory days stay elevated: a write-down like the H20 charge would end both the claim and the margin assumption behind the price.
The record ends with the July 2026 quarter, and the CEO's resignation was filed on 2026-11-12. The record cannot show any effect of that change on margins; only the next 10-Q could.

conditions.text: A quarterly gross margin below 70% in a later 10-Q would end the four-quarter run the claim rests on.
A quarterly operating margin below 50% would break the corollary that should hold if the claim is true.
An inventory balance rising above the $31.57B reported at Q2 FY2027 would add to the build that preceded the last margin collapse.
